questions.question: A DOT-compliant helmet:

options.text: Will severely limit what you can see.
Will let you see clearly to both sides.
Will prevent you from turning your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will let you see clearly to both sides.
questions.explanation: A helmet that meets DOT standards will not restrict your vision. You will be able to see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: When riding, you should wear:
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors so other drivers can see you easily. Reflective materials also help make you more visible.

questions.question: The best clothing for a motorcyclist:
questions.explanation: Good riding clothes protect you if you crash, keep you comfortable, and make you visible to other drivers.

questions.question: If vehicles are on both sides of your motorcycle, which lane position is usually safest?
questions.explanation: Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions. If vehicles are on both sides, the center position is usually the safest choice.

questions.question: Before every ride, you should:

options.text: Check that your brake lights work.
Check that the paint is not peeling.
Make sure the bike is completely clean.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that your brake lights work.
questions.explanation: Always do a safety check before riding. Test your brakes to make sure each brake light works properly.

questions.question: What removes alcohol from your body?
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to remove alcohol. Coffee and exercise cannot speed up this process.

questions.question: Using both brakes:

options.text: Should be done every time you stop.
Should only be done in emergencies.
Should only be done on slippery roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be done every time you stop.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop, not just in emergencies.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that the right lane ends ahead.

questions.question: If you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle:

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlight to tell the other vehicle to go.
Continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop completely and go when it is safe.
Only stop if other traffic is coming.
Vehicles will be entering the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Stop completely, let traffic and pedestrians pass, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: When should you inspect your motorcycle for safety?
questions.explanation: Always inspect your motorcycle before you ride. Small problems on a motorcycle are more dangerous than small problems on a car.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. If you speed up, they may just tailgate you at the higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: What happens when you drink alcohol quickly?

options.text: It builds up in your body faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: It builds up in your body faster.
questions.explanation: When you drink quickly, alcohol builds up in your body faster. Your body removes about one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink per hour, alcohol will stay in your system.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply controlled pressure to both the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.question: How can you reduce fatigue on a long motorcycle trip?
questions.explanation: On a long trip, limit your riding to about six hours per day and take frequent breaks. Wind, cold, and rain can make you tired quickly, so dress to protect yourself from bad weather.

questions.question: What do reflective and brightly-colored helmets and clothing do?

options.text: Should only be worn at night.
Help other drivers see you better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help other drivers see you better.
questions.explanation: Wearing brightly-colored or reflective clothing increases your chances of being seen by other drivers.

questions.question: What should you know about blind spots on motorcycles?

options.text: You should check them before changing lanes.
They do not exist if you have a mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should check them before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks part of your normal routine.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid fatigue on a long motorcycle trip?
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue on a long trip, limit your riding time each day and take frequent rest breaks. Avoid artificial stimulants because you may feel very tired when they wear off.

questions.question: What is most important when buying a motorcycle helmet?
questions.explanation: Protection is most important when buying a helmet. Choose one that fastens securely, fits well, and meets DOT safety standards.

questions.question: What color are service signs?
questions.explanation: Service signs are blue with white letters. They show where you can find rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Look only at what is in front of you.
Look only at what is behind you.
Watch what is both in front of and behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch what is both in front of and behind you.
questions.explanation: You must pay attention to what is ahead of you. But you also need to know what is behind you. Check your mirrors often to stay aware of traffic behind you.

questions.question: When cars are merging from an entrance ramp, a motorcyclist should:

options.text: Assume the entering drivers see them.
Never assume the entering drivers see them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never assume the entering drivers see them.
questions.explanation: Do not assume that merging drivers can see you. Give them plenty of space. Change lanes away from the merging traffic if you can. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to let them merge safely.

questions.question: If you must ride on a slippery surface, what should you do?
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, slow down. Avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes smoothly when you need to stop.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should avoid:

options.text: Keeping their knees against the gas tank while riding.
Keeping their feet firmly on the footrests while riding.
Adjusting the handlebars so their hands are above their elbows.

questions.correctAnswerText: Adjusting the handlebars so their hands are above their elbows.
questions.explanation: Set your handlebars so your hands are level with or below your elbows. This position helps you steer with control. Keep your feet on the footrests and your knees against the gas tank. This helps you balance when turning.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop behind the emergency vehicle on the road.
Stop and wait for the emergency vehicle to move.
Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes to give it extra space. Slow down and be ready to stop as you pass the emergency scene.
